name: Question 17
problem:
A certain company produces $2$ types of flour, flour $A$ and flour $B.$ The following table describes how the number of consumers changes between both types of flour each month:
From:
Flour $A$ Flour $B$
To: Flour $A$ $0.3$ $0.6$
Flour $B$ $0.7$ $0.4$
That is, $70%$ of flour $A$ customers switch to flour $B$ each month, and $60%$ of flour $B$ customers change to flour $A.$ Currently, $6\,000$ customers use flour $A,$ while $4\,000$ customers use flour $B.$ How many customers will use flour $A$ in one month? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
worked_solution:
From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.3 & 0.6 \\ 0.7 & 0.4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of flour is

$$
[\begin{aligned}6\,000 \\ 4\,000\end{aligned}].
$$

Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers $(10\,000),$ we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

$$
{x}_{0}=\frac{1}{10\,000}[\begin{aligned}6\,000 \\ 4\,000\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0.6 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the state vector ${x}_{1}$ after one year, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

$$
{x}_{1}=P{x}_{0}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =P{x}_{0} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.3 & 0.6 \\ 0.7 & 0.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.6 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.42 \\ 0.58\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, after one month, $42%$ of customers will use flour $A.$ Computing $42%$ of $10\,000,$ we obtain

$$
10\,000\cdot 0.42=4\,200.
$$

Therefore, $4\,200$ customers will use flour $A$ in one month.

Question 17
?

A certain company produces 2 types of flour, flour A and flour B. The following table describes how the number of consumers changes between both types of flour each month:

From:
Flour A Flour B
To: Flour A 0.3 0.6
Flour B 0.7 0.4

That is, 70% of flour A customers switch to flour B each month, and 60% of flour B customers change to flour A.

Currently, 6000 customers use flour A, while 4000 customers use flour B. How many customers will use flour A in one month? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

a
5500
b
4800
c
4500
d
4200
e
3800
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix:

P=[0.30.60.70.4]

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of flour is [60004000]. Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers (10000), we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

x0=110000[60004000]=[0.60.4]

To find the state vector x1 after one year, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

x1=Px0

Therefore, we have

x1=Px0=[0.30.60.70.4][0.60.4]=[0.420.58].

So, after one month, 42% of customers will use flour A. Computing 42% of 10000, we obtain

10000⋅0.42=4200.

Therefore, 4200 customers will use flour A in one month.
